summary: The change gives every deferral a drafted issue that the workflow checks at shape and at resolve. Filing is safe to repeat, through a per-round record and a lookup of the draft's last line, and the replies, handoff and cap-hit comment all say where each item went. The correctness findings share one shape: the deferred list and its free-text fields are trusted as written. So an entry beside a decided call, a mitigation phrased in words, a title that cleans to nothing, or a repository with Issues off changes what a round demands, reports or files. The rest are a stale guard doc, prompt wording and small refactors. This repository has no scheduled commands or queued jobs, so there is no overlap to check. The reviewer's guard refuses `node`, so the loop-side findings were traced through the cited lines rather than run.

findings.title: docs/guard.md still describes the after-run deferred-issue filing this PR removed
findings.description: The Hook section still says "The cost is one prompt in the main session too: filing a deferred issue after a run asks once in default mode." This PR removed the skill's after-run triage and its `redline-gh.sh issue-create` call (the removed bullets in the `done` section of skills/redline/SKILL.md; the base skill names `issue-create` once). Deferred issues are now filed during the run by the GitHub agent through `redline-gh.sh defer`, and the skill's Rules say it never runs that (skills/redline/SKILL.md:276). A grep over README.md, docs/, skills/, scripts/ and tests/guard-cases.tsv finds no other reference to the after-run filing. The plan's Docs table (agent-os/specs/2026-11-16-1026-95-defer-means-tracked/plan.md:262-279) does not name docs/guard.md, and the file is not in this diff, so the sentence went stale through this change without being touched.
findings.proposedFix: Update the Hook section of `docs/guard.md`: drop the after-run filing as the example of the main-session prompt, or replace it with what still prompts there now that filing runs inside the GitHub agent, a Redline role.

findings.title: The defer record is read once and written back with no lock, so concurrent defers drop entries
findings.description: `defer` reads the record once (`existing`, lines 573-577). Every write afterwards is `defer_record` of that snapshot plus one entry (lines 585, 597, 611). defer_record (173-179) applies `. + {($id): $e}` to the string it was handed, not to the file as it stands. Nothing locks the record between the read and the write. In issue mode that window holds `gh issue list` and `gh issue create` (593, 604), so seconds of network. If two `defer` runs on the same round's record overlap, each writes its own snapshot and the later write drops the earlier entry. The trigger is the GitHub agent running two drafts' commands at the same time. Its prompt (workflows/redline-loop.js:2205) and agents/redline-github.md:28 tell it to take the drafts in order, so this needs the agent to put both commands in one message and the harness to run them concurrently. The cost shows later: a resume of `file deferred r<n>` (for example after a failed push) finds no entry for the dropped finding and falls back to the GitHub body search. The script calls that search best effort (591-592) and the PR body lists its lag as a known gap, so a second issue can be opened inside that window. I traced the script. I could not run two defers at once: the reviewer's guard allows no such run, and whether the harness runs a role's Bash calls concurrently is not something the repository shows.
findings.proposedFix: Serialise the update: take a lock around the read and the write (for example `mkdir <record>.lock` with a short retry loop, removed on exit), and re-read the record just before writing so the new entry is merged into the file as it stands rather than into the snapshot taken at the start.
findings.wouldConfirm: From a GitHub-agent session, issue two `redline-gh.sh defer issue` commands for different findings on one record in a single message and check whether the record keeps both entries.

findings.title: defer_record's temp file in the record folder is not cleaned up on failure and would be committed
findings.description: defer_record creates its temp file beside the record, inside the round's `redline/` folder (line 176), and sets no trap for it. The script's only trap removes the body file (602). If jq exits non-zero at 177 (`set -euo pipefail` at 148 then exits before the `mv` at 178), or the process is killed between 176 and 178, a `.redline-deferred.XXXXXX` file is left in `<spec folder>/redline/`. commitRecord lists every untracked file under each round's `redline/` folder (`git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all`, workflows/redline-loop.js:2286 and 4413-4427) and commits all of them, so the leftover would land on the branch. The window is narrow. Both jq inputs were produced or validated by jq just before (574, and 584/596/610), so the realistic path is a kill (a stall timeout on the GitHub agent's Bash call) inside a window of milliseconds.
findings.proposedFix: Remove the temp file when the jq step fails or the function is left early, for example an explicit `|| { rm -f <tmp>; exit 1; }` after the jq line together with a RETURN trap. Keep it beside the record so the `mv` stays atomic.

findings.title: With deferTo github, a repository with Issues turned off stops every deferring round at defer, and a resume cannot change it
findings.description: With `deferTo` github (the default, and this repository's own `.claude/redline.json`), filing runs `gh issue list` (593) and then `gh issue create` (604) under `set -euo pipefail` (148). Nothing before that checks that the repository has GitHub Issues on: grep finds no `hasIssuesEnabled` or similar check in scripts/, skills/, workflows/, README.md or docs/. On such a repository the first deferral of a round would make the script exit non-zero. fileDeferred then throws at stage `defer` (workflows/redline-loop.js:3283-3285). That is after the gate passed on the round's commits (the call at 3869 comes before the push at 3909), so the commits stay local and no reply is posted. A resume relaunches with the marker's args exactly (skills/redline/SKILL.md:51-52), so `deferTo` stays github and the same call fails again. The way out is a fresh run with `defer to spec`, and the precheck stops while HEAD is ahead of the PR. The repository code is traced. What it cannot show is gh's behaviour: the installed gh (/opt/homebrew/bin/gh) carries the error text "the '%s' repository has disabled issues", which is its refusal for an issue command on such a repository, but I did not run it against one. #2 (Phase 2: code host and issue tracker providers) is about trackers other than GitHub and does not track this failure.
findings.proposedFix: When deferTo is github and the run posts, read `gh repo view --json hasIssuesEnabled` at launch and stop the launch with one line, or fall back to spec with a warning, when Issues are off. Separately, let `defer issue` record the draft and report it when the issue commands refuse, so a resume is not stuck.
findings.wouldConfirm: Run `gh issue list --state all --search x` and `gh issue create` against a repository with Issues disabled and see each exit non-zero.

findings.title: The three deferTo words are listed separately in three places in redline-prefs.sh
findings.description: The words github, spec and print are written out in three places in this script: the `--defer-to` case (381), MERGE's `deferToWord` def (413), and the `bad_defer` jq filter (441). The workflow keeps its own list as well (DEFER_TO, workflows/redline-loop.js:187). If a fourth word were added to the case and the merge but not to line 441, `resolve` would exit 2 on a valid `deferTo` in redline.json while the merge accepts it.
findings.proposedFix: Define the list once in the script, for example a JSON array passed to both jq programs with `--argjson`, which `deferToWord` and the `bad_defer` filter both test with `IN`, and have the bash case read the same variable.

findings.title: A capped run never lists its deferred items or prints print-mode drafts
findings.description: The `capped` section (line 268) says only to list `openFindings` and stop. The capped result carries `deferred` and `deferTo` like every result, since result() builds the common fields (workflows/redline-loop.js:2494 and 2545-2547; `result('capped', ...)` at 4746), but the skill reads neither there. Printing the print-mode drafts is in the `done` section only (264). The PR's docs promise that with `defer to print` the draft's title and body are printed when the run ends (README.md:61, docs/running.md:126, docs/contract.md:132). So a `defer to print` run that defers in an early round and then hits the cap (the shape of the loop test 'filing: a run that defers, then hits the cap') ends with the drafts' paths in the cap-hit comment and nothing printed in the session. The draft files are still in the spec folders, so nothing is lost, but the paste-ready text the person chose `print` for is never shown, and the session's capped summary does not mention the deferred items at all. Line 266, the section heading, is a context line of this diff. The section body sits just past the hunk.
findings.proposedFix: In the `capped` section, after `openFindings`, list `deferred` one line each as the `done` section does, and when `deferTo` is print, print each draft's `draft.title` and `draft.body` the same way. Or point the section at the `done` section's deferred paragraph.

findings.title: hasMitigation counts any wording of 'nothing ships' other than '' and 'none' as a mitigation
findings.description: hasMitigation (768-771) treats only an empty string and `none` (with an optional note in parentheses and a full stop) as nothing shipping. Any other way of writing nothing, such as `Nothing ships now.`, `N/A` or `No mitigation`, counts as a mitigation. The schema and prompts do tell the shaper and the resolve agent to write an empty string (1906, 1963, 2001; agents/redline-shaper.md:33; agents/redline-resolve.md:23). But the same sentence of the shape prompt asks for the recommendation to be 'the mitigation for a defer or that nothing ships now' (1906), and the code already accepts one non-empty spelling, `none`. Traced for a shaper that writes such a phrase as the mitigation: needCommits demands a commit for the finding (3790-3793), while the plan has no task for it (shape-spec point 7, .claude/commands/agent-os/shape-spec.md:54, gives a task only to a defer that ships a mitigation) and the implementer is told nothing about an empty mitigation applying (2107). judge reports `no commit names R1-n` (2431-2433) and the repair pass gets the same reason. The round then stops at stage check (3839-3841), unless the repair adds a commit that names the id just to satisfy the check. If such a commit lands, outcomesFor keeps it as the mitigation's (2877-2878), the reply reads `deferred to #N. Mitigated in <sha>`, and `bought` counts the deferral as shipping (3934-3939), so a deferral that ships nothing buys a round. On the base branch every defer demanded a commit (`f.disposition === 'defer'` in needCommits), so the split by mitigation text is new in this pull request. The reviewer's guard refuses `node`, so the loop harness was not run. This is traced through the cited lines.
findings.proposedFix: Stop deciding by wording: add an explicit field to DEFERRED_SCHEMA (for example `ships: boolean`) and test that in hasMitigation. Or at least widen the test to the common phrasings of nothing (n/a, nothing, nothing ships, no mitigation). A loop scenario with `mitigations: { 'R1-1': 'Nothing ships now.' }` and `commitIds: [[]]` should then end done with no commit demanded.

findings.title: A title that cleans to nothing gives a draft opening '# ', which redline-gh.sh defer refuses on every resume
findings.description: issueDraft picks the title before cleaning it: `draftTitle(title || item.title)` (1271). A person's title is kept as given (214 trims only `notes`), so a whitespace-only title is truthy, wins over the shaper's, and draftTitle (1257-1260) reduces it to ''. The draft then opens with `# `, which `redline-gh.sh defer` refuses: the check at scripts/redline-gh.sh:557 needs at least one character after `# ` and exits 2. fileDeferred throws at stage defer (3283-3285), either in the round (toFile at 3866) or at Finish (settleHeld, 3378). A resume keeps args.deferrals byte for byte (skills/redline/SKILL.md:52), so it fails again and only a fresh run recovers. A shaper title made only of control characters fails the same way: draftMissing (773) trims it and lets it through, since trim keeps a control character, and draftTitle then strips it. On autopilot that title goes to filing with no stop; on the other dials the stop shows the person an empty title. The conditions are narrow: an empty `<id>: title.` line recorded as a space, or a shaper title of control characters only.
findings.proposedFix: Clean each title before choosing between them: `draftTitle(title) || draftTitle(item.title)` in issueDraft. Have draftMissing (or checkDrafts and the resolve check) treat a title whose draftTitle is '' as missing, so a title that cleans to nothing stops the run at shape or resolve, where the shaper reruns, instead of at filing.

findings.title: Filed and held outcomes are each worded by hand twice, as a clause and as a sentence
findings.description: Where an item went is written in two places. deferredTo (1292) and deferredSentence (1294) state the same filing as a clause and as a sentence, and HELD (2915) and HELD_SENTENCE (2916) do the same for a draft held to the end of the run. A wording change that misses its twin would make a reply and a handoff line describe the same outcome in different words. prior-findings reads the clause form's opening word, `deferred`, back as settled.
findings.proposedFix: Keep one helper per outcome that returns both forms, or build the sentence form from the same parts (number or path, person label) in one function, so the two forms cannot drift apart.

findings.title: An empty-mitigation deferred entry beside a decided call zeroes its fix commits and files an issue for it
findings.description: For a finding with a decision, outcomesFor now records `commits: shipped` (2887). `shipped` is [] whenever the deferred list holds an entry for the id whose mitigation is empty (2873-2878). That happens whether or not the person's decision was a deferral. isDeferral (3663) likewise counts any entry as a deferral once `roundDecisions[id]` exists, without checking that the decision chose one. One way such an entry arises: the person answers a call 'Fix it now'; that decision has no `disposition`, so awayFromDefer (3603) keeps entries. The first resolve plans the fix task. A bounced plan's reshape then re-sorts the answered call's finding as defer with a drafted entry and mitigation '' (the case the comment at 4484-4485, R8-6, says can happen: 'whatever disposition a reshape gave its finding'). The rebuilt list keeps that entry (3723-3724), and the reshape check accepts it (checkCalls skips known calls, 3026-3040; checkDrafts sees a full draft, 3088-3094). needCommits still demands the fix commit through resolved.tasks (3794), and the implementer builds it. Then: draftStop raises a draft for it on guided (3667-3669), and autopilot files it with no question (3863-3869). The reply reads '<notes> No code change. Deferred to #301.' (2936, draftClose 2919) although a commit fixed it. `fixed` leaves the finding out (3940), so when it is the round's only fix, fixedAny is false. The next range is then marked empty (4770): the next round is told it changed no code (1050, 1519), and with coverage off the run hands off as noRecheck (4761-4766), so the fix commit is never re-reviewed. The resolve agent writing a deferred entry with mitigation '' for a call it planned as a fix has the same effect. On the base branch the decided branch used `commits: named` and isDeferral did not exist, so this is new in the diff. Both triggers need an agent to stray from its prompt: the reshape is told a decision the person made stays (1961), and the resolve agent is told to write entries only for a mitigate choice or a defer override. The reviewer's guard refuses `node`, so the loop harness was not run. This is traced through the cited lines.
findings.proposedFix: Let a decision count as a deferral only when it is one: isDeferral should test `roundDecisions[id].disposition === 'defer'`, or that the resolve agent's own entry for the id came from this decision (record which ids its `out.deferred` carried), not the bare existence of a decision. In outcomesFor's decided branch, apply shipsNothing only when the decision is a deferral, and keep `named` otherwise. A loop scenario with `ask: ['R1-1']`, a 'Change it' decision, `resolveDeferred: [{ id: 'R1-1', mitigation: '', ... }]` and `commitIds: [['R1-1']]` on autopilot should post 'Applied in <sha>', make no filing call, and count R1-1 as fixed.

findings.title: fileDeferred always labels its call phase 'Push and reply', including when Finish files held drafts
findings.description: fileDeferred passes `phase: 'Push and reply'` (3281). settleHeld calls it during Finish, after `phase('Finish')` (4199 then 4221, and 4610 then 4611), while the 'deferred replies' call that follows carries `phase: 'Finish'` (3402). So with `defer at end`, `file deferred r<n>` is grouped under Push and reply after Finish has started, which misreports the run's progress to anyone watching or resuming it.
findings.proposedFix: Pass the phase in, `fileDeferred(pass, record, drafts, phaseName)`, with 'Finish' from settleHeld. Keep 'Push and reply' for the in-round call, since the phase is part of the agent options a replay compares.

findings.title: The held replies' prompt says the round pushed its commits even when push is off
findings.description: settleHeld hands pushReplyPrompt the reason 'the round pushed its commits when it ended; these are the replies its deferred items waited for' (3401). pushReplyPrompt puts that into Step 1 as `Do not push (...)` whenever postToGitHub is true (2171). With `no push` (push false, 164) the round never pushed (doPush at 3908 is false), so the prompt states something false about the branch to the GitHub agent, beside replies that may say 'Committed locally; not pushed.' (1464). The agent pushes nothing either way, so no behaviour changes.
findings.proposedFix: Choose the reason from the setting: with push off, say 'push is off for this run; these are the replies its deferred items waited for'. Otherwise keep the current wording.

findings.title: isDeferral rebuilds every effective disposition per entry, and drafts are recomposed at each call site
findings.description: isDeferral (3663) calls effectiveDispositions() (3655-3658), which maps every shaped finding, inside `.some` for each deferred entry it tests. Each filter over the deferred list is therefore entries times findings. draftsOf (3547-3554) recomposes every draft's text with issueDraft (three postedText passes, 1273-1277) on each call. It is called for shaperDrafts (3559), for each draftStop (3668, reached from 3679, 3727 and 3739) and for roundDeferrals (3863). fileDeferred (3278) and deferredEntry (3312) compose the text once more. Small at today's sizes. draftsOf does need the recomposition to detect a changed draft, but the later two calls could read the text already stored in record.drafts when no title of the person's replaces it.
findings.proposedFix: Compute the effective dispositions once per filter (a Set of ids deferred after overrides) and test membership in isDeferral. Have fileDeferred and deferredEntry reuse `record.drafts[id].text` when the title is ''.

findings.title: The inFixDiff claim is checked at file level against the previous plan's paths
findings.description: The workflow honours a fix-diff claim when the finding's file is under a path the previous round's plan named (4659; the paths are kept at 3754). That is a file-level stand-in for a line-level fact, as decision 20 of the spec chose (agent-os/specs/2026-11-16-1026-95-defer-means-tracked/plan.md:47). There are two readings. Too loose: if the verifier wrongly sets inFixDiff on a low-severity bug in the PR's own code, in a file the previous plan also named, the check passes and the bug buys no round. It is still fixed, like a nit. Too strict: a true claim on a file a fix commit changed without the plan naming it is cleared with a warning and buys a round. Such a commit is possible because the PR's files are on the checker's allowed list (3797). Testing against the files changed in range.from..range.to would make the second case exact. It would not settle the first, which only the verifier's statement can.
findings.proposedFix: Either keep the plan-paths test as decision 20 chose and say in docs/running.md (Rounds, step 7) that the check is per file, or test the finding's file against the files the previous round's commits changed (range.from..range.to).

accounting.ref: The claim is that the mock's lazily created scenario.filedRecord leaks between the layout launches that share one scenario object. It does not: go() (tests/loop-test.mjs:324) hands mock() a shallow copy, `s = { ...scenario, ... }`, so line 131 sets filedRecord on that per-launch copy and each layout run starts with no record. A record is shared only when a scenario passes its own filedRecord object, as the two resume scenarios do on purpose (2933, 2935).

list.summary: For a finding the person decided (a judgment call they answered), an empty-mitigation deferred entry beside it zeroes the fix's commits (shipsNothing), and isDeferral counts the entry as a deferral just because a decision exists, without checking the decision was a deferral.
list.failure_scenario: The shaper makes R1-2 an ask and the person answers 'Fix it now'. The first resolve plans a fix task and needCommits makes the gate demand the commit. The plan bounces and the reshape re-sorts the answered call's finding as defer, with a drafted entry and mitigation '' (the R8-6 re-sort case). The rebuilt deferred list keeps that entry. isDeferral(R1-2) is true, so autopilot files an issue for a finding the person decided to fix (other dials stop to show the draft). In outcomesFor, shipsNothing is true, so commits become []. The reply reads '<notes> No code change. Deferred to #301.' although a commit fixed it. `fixed` leaves it out, so fixedAny is false and the next range is marked empty: the next round is told 'round N changed no code', and with coverage off the run hands off as noRecheck. The fix commit is never re-reviewed. The same loss happens when the resolve agent plans a task for a call but writes mitigation ''.

list.summary: The defer record is a read-modify-write with no lock: `existing` is read at the start and later written back as existing plus one entry, so two `defer` invocations on the same pass's record overwrite each other's entries.
list.failure_scenario: A pass defers R2-1 and R2-2, and the GitHub agent issues both `redline-gh.sh defer issue ... round-2-deferred.json` commands in one message, in parallel. Both read `{}`. A records R2-1 (#301), then B writes `{R2-2: #302}` and A's entry is gone. A later resume of `file deferred r2` (for example after the push fails) finds no record for R2-1 and falls back to GitHub's body search, which the script itself calls best effort because the index lags. Inside that window a second issue is opened for R2-1.

list.summary: With the default `deferTo: github`, a repository with GitHub issues turned off makes every defer fail at `gh issue list` / `gh issue create`. Nothing at launch checks whether issues are on, and a resume cannot change deferTo.
list.failure_scenario: Run on a repository with Issues disabled. The round's gate passes, then `file deferred r1` runs. gh exits non-zero ('repository has disabled issues'), so the run stops at stage `defer` after committing and before pushing or replying. A resume relaunches with byte-identical args (deferTo still github) and fails the same way every time. The person has to discard the run and start fresh with `defer to spec`.

list.summary: hasMitigation counts only '' and 'none…' as 'nothing ships'. Common phrasings ('Nothing ships now.', 'N/A', 'No mitigation') count as a real mitigation, and the shape prompt itself uses the words 'that nothing ships now' next to the defer recommendation.
list.failure_scenario: The shaper defers R1-1 with mitigation 'Nothing ships now.' needCommits then demands a commit for R1-1. The plan has no task for it (the implementer is told an empty-mitigation deferral gets none), so judge fails with no commit naming R1-1, the repair pass fails the same way, and the run stops at check. If a commit does land, the deferral wrongly buys a round and the reply reads 'deferred to #301. Mitigation: Nothing ships now.'

list.summary: The `capped` result section only lists openFindings and stops. It never reports `deferred`, and in print mode it never prints the drafts, which only the `done` section does.
list.failure_scenario: Run with `defer to print` and `max 1 rounds`: round 1 defers R1-3, and round 2 finds a correctness bug and hits the cap. The cap-hit comment lists R1-3's draft path, but the session prints neither its title nor its body. The docs say print-mode drafts are printed when the run ends, so the person who chose print never gets the text to paste.

list.summary: args.deferrals titles are taken untrimmed and never checked. A whitespace-only title (or a shaper title made only of control characters, which passes draftMissing's trim) becomes '' in draftTitle, so the draft's first line is '# ', which redline-gh.sh defer refuses.
list.failure_scenario: The person's answer is recorded as {action:'file', title:' ', ...}. `' ' || item.title` keeps ' ' (it is truthy), and draftTitle reduces it to ''. The draft opens with '# ', the script exits 2 ('must open with "# <title>"'), and the run stops at `file deferred r1`. A resume keeps the same args.deferrals, so it fails again and only a fresh run recovers.

list.summary: settleHeld's push-and-reply prompt always tells the GitHub agent 'the round pushed its commits when it ended', even when push is off for the run.
list.failure_scenario: Run with `no push` and `defer at end`. At Finish, Step 1 of the 'deferred replies r1' prompt says the round pushed its commits, which is false (they are local only). The agent is acting on a false fact about the branch state while it posts replies that say 'Committed locally; not pushed.'

list.summary: The inFixDiff claim is checked only by whether the file is in the previous plan's paths. That is a file-level check of a line-level claim, so it can be both too loose and too strict.
list.failure_scenario: Round 1's plan names app/Order.php, and a coverage candidate in round 2 is a bug in the PR's own code elsewhere in that same file. If the verifier wrongly sets inFixDiff, it passes the check and the low-severity bug buys no round. In the other direction, a fix commit that touched a PR file not in the plan list has its true claim cleared. The files changed in range.from..range.to would be the accurate test.

list.summary: The operating doc still says 'filing a deferred issue after a run asks once in default mode'. This PR removed the session's after-run triage and issue-create; deferred issues are now filed by the GitHub agent during the run.
list.failure_scenario: A teammate reading docs/guard.md expects a permission prompt in the main session when deferred issues are filed after a run. That path no longer exists, and `redline-gh.sh defer` runs inside the GitHub agent, so the doc misdescribes what the guard's main-session exception costs.

list.summary: fileDeferred hard-codes phase 'Push and reply', so the filing call settleHeld makes during Finish is labelled under the wrong phase.
list.failure_scenario: With `defer at end`, `file deferred r1` runs inside finish() after phase('Finish'), yet it reports phase 'Push and reply'. /workflows shows the run going back to an earlier phase after Finish has started, which misleads anyone watching or resuming it.

list.summary: defer_record creates its temp file inside the spec folder's redline/ directory. If jq fails or the script is killed between mktemp and mv, a `.redline-deferred.XXXXXX` file is left there, and commitRecord stages every untracked file under the record folders.
list.failure_scenario: The GitHub agent's Bash call is interrupted (stall timeout) right after mktemp. An empty `.redline-deferred.Ab12Cd` stays in agent-os/specs/<round>/redline/, and the run-record commit adds it to the branch.

list.summary: The mock GitHub agent creates scenario.filedRecord lazily on whatever scenario object it is given. Several unrelated launches in the layout block share one `scenario` object, so filing state leaks between independent runs.
list.failure_scenario: 'layout: every outcome in one run' files R1-4 as #301 and stores it on `scenario`. 'layout: no login' and 'layout: no login, a decision with no notes' reuse the same object, so their R1-4 filing comes back reused:true. Those runs do not test a first-time filing, and a regression in reuse handling would be hidden because the number is still 301.

list.summary: isDeferral rebuilds effectiveDispositions(), a fresh array over all shaped findings, for every deferred entry it checks. draftsOf also recomposes each draft's full text (three postedText passes) at each of up to four call sites per round.
list.failure_scenario: Each draftStop() and the filing step does O(entries × findings) work and recomposes every draft's text. It is small today, but it is avoidable: compute the effective-disposition map once per call and keep the composed text that is already stored in record.drafts.

list.summary: deferredTo / deferredSentence and HELD / HELD_SENTENCE are parallel wordings of the same facts, written by hand in two places each.
list.failure_scenario: A future change to how a filed or held item is described has to be made in two strings each. If only one changes, replies and handoff lines describe the same outcome in different words, and prior-findings reads the opening word back. Building the sentence form from one source avoids that.

list.summary: The bad_defer check writes out the three deferTo words again in its own jq, beside MERGE's deferToWord and the bash case for --defer-to.
list.failure_scenario: Adding a fourth destination means editing three separate word lists in one script. Missing the bad_defer list would refuse a valid redline.json value at launch (exit 2) while the merge accepts it.
